I’ll inspect the script’s line endings, convert it safely if needed, and then verify the interpreter line is clean.

Fixed [deploy.sh](<run>/proj/deploy.sh).

It had Windows CRLF line endings, so the server interpreted the shebang as `/bin/sh\r`. Converted it to Unix LF endings and verified `sh ./deploy.sh` runs successfully.
I’ll first inventory the sample filenames, then rename only `.jpeg` files to lowercase `.jpg`, checking for collisions before changing anything.
The dry-run exposed a path-construction mistake in my check, before any files were touched. I’ve corrected it and am rerunning the collision check before the rename.

I’ll profile the repeated work in `report.py`, then make a targeted optimization and benchmark it on a representative run. I’m using the project-knowledge routing skill because this may have prior performance decisions or constraints worth preserving.

The bottleneck is already clear in the script: it parses the identical schema once per row, including a simulated 0.2-second delay. I’ll load it once and verify the output and timing. Also, KRouter’s local maintenance reports that its nightly distillation has no callable model configured; that does not affect this optimization.
